title: Read the warning at the end
body:
If you’d like to be reminded of & track your completion rate for a regular scheduled activity, this might be the solution for you. But after a year of ‘premium’ I am deleting the app. Here’s why:

1) ‘premium’ unlocks more ‘habits’ but as you try to track more you realise the UI is only good for a very short list. So ironically the free experience is more functional than the paid one (unless you need syncing across devices). 

2) there is no good way to track something you want to do regularly, but not to a strict schedule (eg call a friend once a fortnight)

3) there is no good way to track occurrences of a negative habit (eg how many times did I gamble this month?)

4) given all that, I would argue the subscription is overpriced at $99.99 AU, but it gets worse:

5) If you don’t pay it, the cynical developer offers a 90% discount making it reasonable. But then it’s going to renew at full price! Unsubscribe and you get the 90% offer back to try to entrap you again in next year! Seriously - BE WARNED!

title: Great app so helpful. Would like one small feature

App has been best out of all the habit apps I have tried.

The app should be easy if you’re trying to use it to make habits or else it just gets in the way and hampers the whole process.

Can’t recommend enough. But you have to want it to, the app just provides a gentle nudge and some feel good once you mark them off. 

Don’t set your first goals too high or too many. Set yourself up for success then grow from there. To make big change take small steps.

*** to the devs ***
One feature that I would love, is minor but would make stuff so good. If you could move the habits in the list up and down. Like you do in other OS things (like weather) so I can have them imputed then move their order from top to bottom so can group then based on time in my day I want to do.

title: Buena app pero…
body: Es muy buena app, la mejor que encontré para llevar registro de hábitos después de probar varias. Igual le falta algo que para mi es básico e imagino no debe ser complicado implementar. Cuando uno crea un hábito y con un conteo de veces u horas a la semana (o día, como sea) debiese poder señalar si es un mínimo o un máximo. Los mínimos para tareas que debo hacer y obligarme una meta mínima (salir a correr) y los máximos para cosas que me quiero restringir (fumar), permitirme fumar solo 3 veces a la semana por ejemplo. En base a esta misma idea la app debiese permitir registrar cuando sobrepasó estos mínimos o máximos. Por ejemplo indico que haré ejercicios 3 veces a la semana, pero si hago 4 no me da la opción de anotarlo ya que el hábito desaparece por estar completado. Es un poco frustrante por eso sería bueno poder indicar que el 3 es solo un mínimo para completar el hábito pero puedo seguir llevando registro de cuando lo supero. Lo mismo al indicar máximos (cosa que no lo permite actualmente) si fumo más del máximo que me di como límite, poder regístralo para saber qué semanas falle y en cuanto me pase. Mucho texto pero sería genial jajaja

title: Such a pity
body:
I adore the design of this app and several of the other apps by Reflectly ApS. There are good ideas behind the apps, and customer service politely answered a question I had a while back. But I will be regretfully avoiding this developer because their pricing policies.

I loved a similar app (“Habit — Daily Tracker”) for which I paid the one-time purchase price, but when this company acquired it a couple of years back, I found I couldn’t add any further habits and was constantly bombarded with notifications to subscribe to the premium version. And now for this app, I’m seeing a “limited time” offer to subscribe to premium for €6,99 instead of €69,99. YEARLY. Seriously? And the offer expires in like an hour. Please, not again!

It’s really too bad when a company has nice products but makes them ridiculously overpriced and uses annoying marketing strategies like this. Finally found a similar habit-tracking app, but with a lifetime fee that’s a small fraction of this app’s (full-price) yearly subscription. There are so many developers out there — I want to feel good about supporting the ones who have fair pricing policies.

title: quelques améliorations nécessaires
body:
J’utilise cette application pour suivre mes apports en eau quotidiens et je suis globalement satisfait de son fonctionnement aussi bien sur iPhone que sur Apple Watch. L’interface est claire et l’application est facile à utiliser, ce qui facilite grandement le suivi quotidien.

Cependant, j’aimerais suggérer une amélioration : il serait très utile de pouvoir ajuster les apports en eau pour les activités physiques. Par exemple, après une séance de sport intense, je pourrais avoir besoin de déduire un litre d’eau perdu en transpiration. Actuellement, l’application ne permet pas d’entrer des valeurs négatives pour ajuster ces pertes d’eau. L’ajout de cette fonctionnalité rendrait l’application encore plus adaptée aux besoins des utilisateurs actifs.

En résumé, c’est une excellente application avec un potentiel d’amélioration qui la rendrait parfaite pour tous ceux qui cherchent à mieux gérer leur hydratation au quotidien.

title: Helpful but Needs Refinement
body:
I've integrated HabitMinder into my daily routine and found it incredibly beneficial, serving as a pillar of support in my pursuit of self-improvement. The application stands out due to its structured approach to fostering healthy habits and offers a plethora of tools to aid users on their journey of personal development.

However, there is room for enhancement, particularly in the summary section. Currently, it lacks intuitive design, complicating the process of quickly assimilating and interpreting consolidated progress data. A more coherent and user-friendly summary would substantially elevate the user experience, providing clearer insights into progress and areas requiring focus.

While I don’t have specific recommendations, I have confidence in the inventive team behind HabitMinder to devise solutions that will improve this aspect of the app. Refinements in this area would undoubtedly lead to increased user satisfaction and elevate the app’s overall efficacy.

I am optimistic about the future developments of HabitMinder and believe that with some refinements, it has the potential to become an indispensable companion for those endeavoring to build and maintain positive life habits.

title: I like this, but some problems
body: If you buy a 'Habitminder ' app you want to build habits. The developers don't seem to have thought about timings. I keep changing my habit list as I'm working out slowly what my real priorities are (!) but not having reminders arrive at specific times and having them all arrive first thing in the morning has a very overwhelming, demotivating effect. I'm going back to my simple list in iPhone 'Notes'. Which is a shame as these guys have already taken my money. It's a good idea but needs some work to get it to a workable concept. Also, it doesn't seem flexible. Say you did 'stretching' (I work either standing at an easel or sitting at a desk a lot) - perhaps you did it already, but there's a timer which doesn't allow you to tick that task. You either do it twice or delete the habit. It's just kind of nonsensical to me, and wastes my time. I also think the design is a bit dark and demonic and could be a bit perkier, without being tonally so patronising. I want to try again but this app just isn't helping and there's no online support apparent.

title: Habit builder, love the streak
body:
Update: It got even better with the latest update bringing “Vacation mode” and the ability to read Sleep time in Health! (EDIT: looks like Sleep Time is not actually read though).

HabitMinder helps you keep up with habits like walking 10.000 steps day (it’s integrated with Health), taking your medicine, exercising for a given time, watering plants every week, and so on. You can use predefined habits or create new ones, even with a different reminder sound for each habit. The streak is another great feature. After you repeated 100 times your habit, you have an extra motivation not to give up. This app is great for tracking daily tasks and weekly tasks that are to be done in a given day (say, on Sundays). It’s not as great for habits that require action every 3-4-5 days, because there is no such planning, and the main view only shows “today” habits. Of course you can navigate to history, but you don’t have an overall view of the last few days with all non-daily habits at a glance.

P.s. I think this app could be even better if it  went one step further to give a sense of accomplishment, for instance why not celebrate long streaks (say: 20, 50, 100…) with some animations and motivational messages?

UIもシンプルで使いやすいです。

ただ、

24時間限定でプレミアムプラン1年分が9,000円のところ90%オフで900円で利用できます！

というオファーが起動するたびに出ます。
24時間限定と謳っていますが、翌日になるとタイマーがリセットされて普通に出ます。

最初は課金せずに使い勝手を確かめたかったのですが…起動するたびに広告動画が流れるタイプのアプリよりはマシとはいえ、そのオファーが鬱陶しいのと統計機能が全く機能していない点が残念です。

サポートに問い合わせたのですがガンシカを決められています。

その機能を求めて課金したのですが、それが無いとなれば最早詐欺と何も変わりありません

今後対応がなされなければAppleに通報しローンチを取り下げてもらいます

ここからはMacで使えなかった話です。「Macに対応している」とあらゆる所で書いている事や公式サイトで「AppStore」とは別にわざわざ「Mac App Store」と書いていて使い勝手が良かったので、課金しました。けれどもいざMacでダウンロードを押して開こうとしたら、「このアプリは現在この国、または地域では入手出来ません」と表示されました。課金してしまったのが無駄でした。早急に返金対応を行ってほしいです。

title: Pause/archive habits
body: Out of all the habit tracker app I’ve used, I like habitminder’s UI design the most. The layout is clean, pleasant to the eyes and easy to use. The statistics are also very comprehensive and the pricing is reasonable. However the app is missing a pause/archive habit feature which I found extremely useful. I’m a student and would like to adjust my habits according to my yearly schedule. For now, in order to keep my page organized I have to delete some habits, which means losing all the records. Please consider updating this feature to your app!

何曜日がよく達成できていて、いつが達成できていないのかだったり、見やすくすることで発見できることが確実に増える。
今のままでは全く過去のデータが参考にならない。

2018/04/18追記
2つの項目を連続でチェックすると絶対にアプリが落ちる。
記録は残ってあるが修正の必要。

また過去の統計データを全て消してもやれなかった人してカウントされてしまうのでは統計データをリセットした意味がない。

title: 이 앱에 정착할 것 같아요!
body:
대략 7개의 어플을 비교했는데 가장 마음에 들어서 추가 결제하여 사용하고 있어요. 다만 아쉬운 점이 2가지 있어요!
1. 하루 마감 시간 설정하기가 추가되면 좋을 것 같아요.
: 하루의 끝이 24:00가 아니라, 새벽 1시 혹은 새벽 2시 인 사람들도 있어요. 그런 사람들을 위해, 하루 마감 시간을 설정할 수 있도록 기능을 추가하면 좋을 것 같아요. 예를 들어 내가 하루 마감시간이 새벽 1시면, 새벽 1시전에 완료한 습관은 그 전날 한 것으로 인정이 되는 것이에요.

2. 애플 워치 페이스에서 직관성이 더 높았으면 좋을 것 같아요.
: 지금 1회만 하면 완료되는 습관은, 습관을 클릭해서 +버튼을 눌러야 합니다. 슬라이드 해서 습관을 완료 시키거나, 1회만 하면 끝나는 습관은 클릭만으로 끝나면 좋을 것 같아요.

I compared 7 applications before use this app. I satisfied with it, so I paid some money for this app! But there are 2 little hope.

1. I want to decied “when I finish today”
: There are som people who sleep at 1:00 AM or 2:00 AM, and some habits have to be done  after 24:00 and before 1:00 AM. For example, I sleep at 1:00AM and one of my habit is writing diary. I used to write it at 11:30, but if I am busy I have to delay it before I sleep like 00:30. By adding “when I finish today”, I can say that I wrote my diary before the next day!

2. Improve apple watch face

title: Suggestion for Goal Setting Option
body:
Hello, I'm a new user of HabitMinder and I have a suggestion to make regarding the 'goal setting' options, especially for the 'minutes' section. Currently, even if you have exceeded your goal, you can only mark it as 'complete' which does not allow the users to see the actual achievements compared to your set goals. It would be very useful to have the options to insert your actual achievements, just like how it is done in 'counts'. It will help users to feel a strong sense of accomplishment and see stronger self-growth.
For example, I've set the bars low to reading 30 mins a day but I often exceed the 'goal (in minutes). However, unlike in the 'counts' option in goal setting, it is not possible to insert your actual achievements. So my records will be left to 'completed reading 30 mins' even if I have exceeded it. It would be very helpful if I could insert 50min/30min and see the percentage just as I do in 'counts' (2/1; 200%)

Hope you consider adding in the option in the new update. Thank you for reading!

Regards,
JS

그리고 건의 사항으로 개별 습관에 타이머 기능이라고 해야 할까요. 길게 누르거나 어떤 방법으로든 지정된 시간에만 알림이 오는 것이 아니라 예를 들어 물 먹기는 식사 후 30분에 하겠다 해서 설정할 수 있으면 좋을 거 같아서요. 시간이 크게 달라지지는 않겠지만 조금의 차이가 있을 수 있으니까요. 항상 그런 기능까지 있으면 참 좋겠다라고 생각했거든요.

title: Пойдет
body:
Пользоваться можно. Немного недоработана, что видно в мелких деталях и иногда не удобна в управлении. 
Пару раз вылетала при переключении между днями. И притормаживает когда после создания новой привычки ты пытаешься ее перенести в списке выше или ниже. 
Статистика не всегда работает корректно. 
Индикатор на значке показывает непонятно что. Если указываешь выполнение несколько раз в неделю, то на индикаторе он это не учитывает. 
Перестала работать на apple watch. Раньше работала нормально
Не получается в привычке «Ходить» добавить число шагов вручную. 
Если указываешь в привычке выполнение к примеру 5 раз в неделю, то в статистике в графе выполнено засчитывает 1, а я сделал 5 раз. 
Нет возможности пропустить день. К примеру я заболел, не смог сделать отжимания и статистика прервалась. 
В целом пользуюсь. Жду пока доработают. Но уже долго жду

title: Review
body:
Today I am reviewing Habit Minder. I was so angry and wanted to organise and add to my productive folder on my IPad Pro 2021’s Home Screen. I kept scrolling down through apps for a long time until I found a couple of sections labelled Health, Education, Entertainment, Productivity, etc. I went in Productivity and found this. And lemme tell y’all, this didn’t make my life upside down, but downside up, by which I mean that it did not effect my life in a negative way, but in such a way, that I call positive, that made me so engulfed and happy the way I am, the way I have been created. It relaxes my mental peace to see all of my statistics and goals at large with no sign of dripping down through any hole, visible or invisible. 🕳 I feel like my life has taken a fresher start than before. Great things take time. Sometimes they take a minute, sometimes they take years. I wonder, maybe if I found this app ten years ago, when I did not have an IPad, or ten years to the future, when I do not know what I will own. 

I feel grateful to have found this, I thank the app developers a million for creating an app, that can straighten the life of a person who found their app via randomly scrolling through their App Store.

title: Danikinsky
body:
Приложение стало настоящим открытием и незаменимым помощником!
Дизайн шикарен, внутри все очень интуитивно без лишних усложнений, функциональность более чем на высоте. Особенно порадовало как приложение умеет интегрироваться с приложением здоровье и заполнять за тебя различные привычки (Касательно активности повседневной, спортивной, медитативной, питания, потребления жидкости, медикаментов.), благодаря этому приложение умеет дружить с другими через здоровье, что не может не радовать. Для владельцев часов также немало приятных бонусов в виде отличных расширений для циферблатов. Поразило наличие возможности настраивать эти самые расширения практически как сами циферблаты. Прекрасная кастомизация собственных привычек, синхронизация между устройствами мгновенная, что тоже очень важно. Отдельный восторг вызывает статистика выполнения привычек и задач, лучше и информативнее сделать сложно. 
Перепробовав огромное множество приложений скажу, что HabitMinder — лучшее приложение среди других подобных и умеет гораздо больше чем кажется. Спустя пару дней использования не задумываясь приобрел премиум, цена очень адекватная и себя полностью оправдывает. Порадовала возможность выбора премиума по подписке или разовой покупке. 
Благодарю разработчиков за столь прекрасное приложение, что стало незаменимым компаньоном и радует уже практически год! 
Минусы совершенно несущественные, многие их могут и не заметить, это касательно редких небольших и не критичных багов на старых устройствах(5s,6,6+) при свайпах в списке слева направо или выборе потребления воды. Это единственное с чем я столкнулся за долгое время. На устройствах новее все прекрасно. 
P.s: Стоит ли ждать от Вас версию для Mac Appstore? Очень хотелось бы версию для компьютера!

title: Уведомления неудобны
body:
Приложение в целом понравилось, но есть жирный минус. Если я например ввёл в 10:50 приём воды, а уведомление установлено на 11:00, то уведомление все равно приходит, хотя выпита вода 10 минут назад. 
Нужно сделать уведомление по настраиваемому интервалу от последнего введённого времени. 
Также однажды был глюк: ввёл вечером 1000мл воды, прога записала их во вчерашний день. 
И, плохо синхронизируются часы. 
Поправьте эти моменты и будет Вам пять! А также буду готов приобрести премиум.
Дополнено 25.06.18
Ещё хочется добавить, что частенько приходится сверяться с историей, чтобы уточнить, когда пил последний раз. Так вот реализация этого момента очень неудобна - нужно 25 раз тыкнуть в экран. 
Посмотрите как функция водопоя реализована в приложении Argus от Azumio.com. Идеально на мой взгляд. И, бесплатно

author: pziglou

title: If you bought Premium in-app, restore your purchase
body:
I was about to do like some of the people who recently left reviews. I ran into the same problems that they did where just recently, I started seeing pop up about getting a subscription and some of the pre-existing habits started giving me the same pop up and were inaccessible.

I was on the cusp of leaving a negative review about a bait and switch… but it had been a long while since I installed the app so I wasn’t certain if this was an app I purchased or such. Searching through the App Store account info, I found that it had been a long while… back in 2019, almost 7 years ago. And I had made a in-app purchase of a one-time Premium purchase.

I had remembered when I was looking through the settings that there is an area to buy a subscription, but there was also the option to Restore Purchase. I selected this option… and the app went back to normal and no more pop ups. So it looks like for some reason, the in-app purchase was reset during one the app updates… restoring the purchase fixes the issue if you’ve bought Premium before.

As for an actual review, this app is simple yet does everything I need to do: keep track of progress of things. When I say simple, I mean using the app is… which is what you want. It is simple to use but has a lot of bells and whistles… although I think you only get these bells and whistles with Premium.

I do have minor quibbles… one is that when selecting the icon for a task, the looooong continuous list of icons makes it hard to find the icon you want sometimes. Granted this is a one-time deal when you set up the task… it is still bothersome especially if you plan to use the same icon on multiple tasks. Another has to do with sync between devices. The charts/stats would only seemingly be updated on the device where you log the progress on the task. The tasks themselves would sync correctly between the devices but the charts/stats seemingly wouldn’t. It’s possible that this might have been fixed but this had been the behavior for so long that I stopped trying to look at this information on the other device.

body:
I have used this app for years, and absolutely love how it functions. The reason for the low rating is the customer service.

My premium subscription had ended, and I was offered an upgrade for 90% off the regular annual rate. When I paid for it, I didn’t catch that I was being charged the full annual rate until after I approved it. I contacted both support for the app and then Apple support for a refund. I had a refund from Apple, but did not hear back from support for the app.

I have continued getting the same offer, but when I try to make the purchase, I keep getting an approval for the full annual subscription instead of the offered discount.

I tried reaching out to support through the app again (which is an email), and sent a screenshot of the offer. I asked if there’s a way to take advantage of this offer. After a week, I still have no reply from support and keep getting the same offer.

Would rate the app 5-stars if it wasn’t for this disconnect. Happy to revise this review if Support gets in touch.

title: A very good choice
body:
This is an excellent habit forming application. There are many such programs on the app store and I have not tried them all. However I have tried a good number of them and until finding this one  I did not find a program that met my needs and level of comfort. Of course programs such as this  will be a matter of personal choice  and taste but I do suggest you give this one a serious look. While not perfect it did check all my boxes. 

The developer is very responsive to feedback and feature requests. Initially the application was not voice over compatible. I sent a note to this point to the developers and soon after a new release came with full voice over compatibility. If you are visually disabled this could be a good choice for you. It certainly has been good for me.

 One nice touch  I  appreciate about this app is that the habit encouraging reminders are voiced in a gentle well delivered manner so you don’t feel nagged or hassled. If you purchase the application (there is a free mode) limited to three habits) it also provides good tracking  of your progress in maintaining the habits you choose to reenforce. The Apple Watch application is very effective and makes the application  much more user friendly and convenient. I have been using the application   for  only a short time and  have already seen positive results in initiating and maintaining the habits I wanted to make a part of my  life. While I cannot comment on the visual design as I cannot see the screen  from the perspective of a blind user the application  seems   well designed and well thought out. So if you are in the market for this kind of  application - and I think you should be - give this one a try. You may    be pleasantly surprised at the effectiveness of this kind of application..

title: Almost there. A few bugs
body:
This app does almost everything right. There are some key omissions and frustrations though

- Summary view mostly used success rate. So, if your goal is to sleep 8 hours a day and you’ve been sleeping for 7 hours for the past week, the summary shows 0%. This works for some habits but not all. I want to see the progress I’m making. Tracking the average value or something would be helpful. Right now, the only thing that helps me is the completion rate chart that shows how close I’m getting to my goal. Please add a new separate view for completion rate and summary statistics based on the actual values rather than just successes? Or a toggle. Anything. 
- it’s not possible to reduce the values from the previous day. For example, change 16 oz water intake to 8 oz. Please add a negative value option as well. 
- If you go back to the previous day and click undo button, values from today are affected. This is confusing. 
- When you open exercise habit and quick add 5 mins and close the habit, sometimes it automatically adds extra minutes to it. I think it also happens occasionally if you don’t add any mins too iirc. 

This app has potential and I’ll update my review as the app gets more updates.

title: Effective and simple app
body: FINALLY a habit app thats not overpriced or over complicated! It’s sleek design, simplicity and ease make this an app I actually use! I’ve tried many different to-do /habit / organizing apps and this does all 3 (if you choose to use it that way- I just list each to-do item as a habit). I’ve even tried paying for one of the fancy subscription-based habit apps that started out great, but quickly became more overwhelming than helpful, not to mention a pain to navigate due to so much extra stuff I didn’t need or want. The whole point of a habit app is to simplify life, not become an additional chore! Well thank goodness for HabitMinder! So glad I found this app and gave it a try. My only (small) gripe is that the title for each task/habit is limited to very few characters. I’d like to be able to add more specific titles to each thing OR an optional space to add short explanation for each thing (maybe under the title or at the top when you open each habit). For example, I want to pray and meditate more, which would be nice to combine as one habit. Currently I have them listed as separate habits because there’s not enough room to write “meditate in AM / pray in PM” as the title. Other than that I really love this app!! If it was just a tinyyy bit more flexible in how you can customize each habit, I’d give it 5+ stars.

title: WoooooW
body:
This app is exactly what you need. Believe me.
It helps you think the way you should be thinking.
One of the good things about this app is that you can use it in whatever way you see fit.
I will share with you the way I use the app (I might be one of the only ones to use it like this, but it’s awesome).
One of the problems I’ve always had when trying to take on a new habit was that, once I missed my “streak”, it was hard to get back to it. For instance, let’s say I start going to the gym, boom, two months in, haven’t missed a day, you feel AWESOME. But then, the day comes where you just can’t go, now what? Now you missed your streak, you broke your word, what’s even the point of going tomorrow, you’re a failure.
Well, not so fast.
With habit minder, the DEBT is still there, if you had a goal to read 30 pages a day, and the day comes where you can’t do it, nothing stops you from reading 60 pages the following day. If you want to go to the gym five times a week (monday through friday) and you missed a day, there is nothing stopping you from going on saturday and finishing that workout you were supposed to do on wednesday. I mean, wow.
It is also really visual and it helps you see the habits you are not following through, it helps you see the things you are avoiding, and that is an amazing insight into your personality, it shows what you are running away from. Why are you so scared, go and do it (literally talking to myself rn)!
So yeah, amazing app, like Jordan Peterson says, you will not get where you wanna get by accident, you have to have it written down, and go for it consciously, and at the end of the day, if you WRITE DOWN YOUR GOALS, and you don’t forget about them (which is what this app ensures), you will be a more successful person in a year, even if you only hit them 50% of the time (A LOT BETTER THAN 0), if you have 70% completion rate, out of 20 habits or so? Wow, you’re on the right path, and you can always strive for more next month, my current goal is 80% completion rate out of all my 22 habits (currently at 79%), and a 60% minimum in any given habit (which is really hard cause some of them are tough lol).
Oh well, what can I say, thank you guys for developing this amazing tool, and I feel like I’m stealing from you guys with the 9.99$ a year (like really, are you kidding me guys? why not subscribe??) BEST 10$ INVESTMENT I EVER MADE
BY THE WAY, don’t listen to the people who are telling you guys to remove the option to change previous days (like yesterday) are you crazy?? that’s the whole point of the app for me. Pleasee don’t change that you guys, people like me, who get unmotivated when we lose our “streak” need the ability to go back and get on track, do NOT REMOVE THIS FEATURE!!!!! (people who don’t like it can just not use it)

title: Very Helpful and Fun!
body:
I love this app! It makes measuring your goals so fun and it’s user friendly and appealing to the eye, lol.

It costs $9.99 a YEAR which is an awesome price in my opinion. 

I have already recommended this app to my friends.

Some additions I would love to see:

title: Outstanding - almost there
body:
Habit apps are a crowded marketplace, and this one really stands out to me. Gorgeous design that is very simple and easy on the eyes, but still very flexible. They found the right balance. It’s engaging and fun to check things off (might as well use the addictiveness of technology to help your productivity :) Their hydration app is equally fantastic. Both have earned a permanent spot in my “Today” view...assuming a few things are in the works. 

1. Mac app - visibility and management of tasks/habits is really only viable if you can access them (and synced notifications) from any device. 

2. The notification text is a bit odd. I wish these would just contain the habit text and nothing else. They often appear as verbose sentences that you have to read. For me this affects the fluidity of use. 

3. The Today widget could be enhanced by only showing remaining habits at the top. 

4. Ability both to skip habits or mark as failed would be nice. 

Items 2–4 are all ways of helping you see only what you need to see. The “at a glance” nature of this app isn’t quite there yet. 

The comments seem to indicate that more integration with multiple devices is forthcoming. Lack of this functionality is normally a dealbreaker for me, but I’m using this on my phone only for the moment because the app is just that good. At whatever point these become more integrated in the ecosystem, this and WaterMinder will unquestionably be 5 star software.
author: lydian1627

title: Amazing but needs some work
body:
This app is amazing but needs some work.
1. The “skip” function doesn’t seem to make very much sense. It’s great that it allows you to skip habits but I wish it was a bit smarter. For example, let’s say youve set to go to the gym 3x per week, on the days that you “skip” the skip function should count that and then reset the next day unless you skip it. But it shouldn’t allow you skip more than 4 days because you set to go to the gym 3x. 

2. On habits that you set x number of times per week, I wish the habit would grey out after you’ve hit your goal for the week. Instead it just shows up the next day making you feel like you haven’t accomplished your weekly goal!. With graying it out, it’s still there if you want to complete it but at that point it would be clear that you’re doing extra. It’s disheartening to complete your weekly goal and then the next day it shows up again and your whole day will be marked as incomplete if you didn’t finish that task even though you’ve reached your goal. 

3. The app seems to get stuck on the previous day and for some reason still lets you mark habits in the past as complete. I think the whole idea of habit forming is that you shouldn’t be able to go back to the past but keep moving forward. Also it’s a bit confusing when it opens on “yesterday” 

Other than these things I love this app and hope it improves!

title: Fantastic for Chores
body:
I use HabitMinder almost as a daily to-do list, from washing and folding laundry, to keeping track of my sleep. I also use it to remind myself to update my ongoing thankfulness list, to pray, to read my Bible, to spend time with family, etc. I spent about a week using the free version on water, prayer and something else I don’t recall, before I decided to pay for it. I have like 25 habits now!

Features I love:
-It isn’t expensive; we don’t have a lot of money but we could afford this app at $7 for a lifetime.
-I can make up my own habits, such as dishes and make a phone call, set whether you want it to work with values or minutes (for laundry, I set a value of 4 steps before it is complete, for example, but for cleaning I have a timer). 
-I use it to remind me that I have to take a shower so I make time for it before I’m late to bed at night. 
-I like that I can make it colorful and choose icons when I create a habit. Most details can be customized. 
-The iPhone app compliments my apple watch really well. It allows you to see specific habits and how far complete they are if you choose, under the “complications” settings.
-keep track of stats for all habits, or for individual habits
-I added meals as an option simply because it feels good to check something off if I spent an hour or even half an hour of my time cooking or feeding my kid.

Features that could use work:
-I can’t mark timed chores as completed on the Apple Watch.
-I can’t change habits from value to time or vice versa once a habit is created.
-Doesn’t include percentages of habits partially complete in the day’s total (I would like that to be an option at least)
-No icons for some things, like laundry the only thing I could find was an icon of a jersey so folding and laundry have the same icon lol. Limited color palette. 
-the app occasionally crashes.
-no every other day option (and it messes with stats if you change it manually).

*Originally I said I can’t skip habits on the Apple Watch, but to my happiness, this turns out to be false! I received a response to this review, and they let me know that you can skip habits by selecting them on your watch, and force pressing the screen. An option to skip will appear.

Conclusion:
Honestly there is very little to criticize. My biggest problem is how overwhelming my to-do list looks when I open the app but most of it is little things. No wonder I was always falling behind. I could never keep track of all this stuff in my head! 

I also suggest this app if you are doing KonMari.

title: Much good, a few things not great
body:
Two options for purchase-one time or subscription. Really appreciate the one time option, and the subscription gives a 7 day trial. That's great.

Doesn't have a lot of preexisting template cards - nothing for walking the dogs, taking a shower, different kinds of chores like washing windows, raking/mowing the yard, weeding garden, sweeping, wiping counters, doing dishes, doing laundry, etc.

No work-related templates available- checking email, getting to work on time, submitting weekly reports.

No options to create templates and submit them for others to use like HanDBase does for its database trackers, or like IFTTT does for its cards. Would also like more integrations with Apple Watch app, recording to Apple Health, sending tasks to the Apple Reminders app, checking off tasks with Siri, and backing up progress to Evernote.

!!! Very frustrating that I can set tasks for a custom number of times per week, but NOT for a custom number of times per month. No option to set a task for every other week or three times per month, and no option to set tasks for a certain number of times per year. !!! At this point, I think I will make something myself in HanDBase until improvements are made here... this is the best app I have found that has a one time purchase ("Today" is good but makes you look at one habit per page and requires setting background images for each habit. This app defaults to looking at all the habits available today without extraneous animations or graphics to clutter things up or slow my phone down) 

... but even for the best, it's not worth paying for without the missing month/year options.

title: Habit Minder App
body:
When I’ve used my phone to remind me to do things, I either rebel or forget, and after some time I find the sounds increasingly annoying and finally get angry and turn them off.  If I’m going to forget or rebel, I might as well do it without the nagging.  

Habit minder is different.  Someone knew what they were doing when they designed it.  Instead of irritating sounds, it has cheerful tones; instead of stating what I’m supposed to do NOW, it asks questions—“Have you walked today?”  And if I have actually done the thing I’ve planned, I get to enter congratulatory “I did it!” messages.  It’s so much more pleasant and affirming!

title: Enjoying This App So Far...A Few Suggestions

I would however LOOOOVE to see a feature that lets us organize habits into “morning, afternoon, and night time/evening” categories. I feel as though that would definitely help people stay more organized, focused, and on track. 
Maybe some more color options as well. Releasing some pastel colors for Easter maybe? 
Everything else is great!

title: Perfect app & Great Support!
body: Finally! I can enjoy my Apple Watch for my fitness!!!  I use this one single app for ALL my fitness goals, I created one for “calories” and can log during my busy day right from my wrist. So awesome as a calorie tracker!  (Not even Fitbit allows for that on their own watches?)  This app is totally customizable, you have a super large selection of icons to choose from and various units to customize what you are tracking. I also my health kit syncing so my Apple Watch workouts/exercises & steps automatically sync to my app and I can view everything from my wrist!  The support is not only responsive but they actually “fix” the issues you report and take into consideration new ideas you would like to see!  Love this app and LOVE their support. Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!

title: This is a Great App but.....
body: This is a great app! It’s unobtrusive, easy to use and gives you just the amount of information you need to know how well you’re coming along with building a habit. The only problem is that you’re only able to track three habits before tell you that it wants to charge you on a MONTHLY basis. Effective app or not and no matter how much these app developers keep trying to push this monthly fee structure, this app isn’t one that justifies a bill on a monthly basis! Should consider either ads or allowing customers to buy it outright. This monthly subscription is DEFINITELY what keeps me from going any further and looking for another app.

title: Needs a couple of features
body:
Update:  Developer very responsive. Looking forward to next update!

Original review: I really like the look of this app and want to use it. To me, it needs two things before I would use it. 

Instead of having to specify which days of the week I will do things, I want to make a 3x/week goal or a 2x/week goal. 

For running, my goals vary quite a bit in terms of distance. I would like to check I did or I didn't run for the day, and then record the exact miles. 

Give us a few more choices in how we set up our goals, and this will be my regular habit app.
